correspondences.feature: West corner of the 20-ft alley mouth where it meets the NORTH (sheet-29 side) line of 22nd Street - the alley carrying the 20-in. water main
correspondences.why_unambiguous: The 20-ft mid-block alley between Av. H East and Av. I East is the ONLY place on either sheet where a 20-inch water main runs north-south, and the 22nd St main changes diameter from 16 in. (west) to 12 in. (east) at exactly this junction, with a hydrant beside it. Both sheets print all four annotations. One block west is a 70-ft named avenue (Av. H East); one block east is Av. I East. No other alley crossing looks like this.

correspondences.feature: North-west corner of the Av. H East / 22nd St intersection = south-east corner of the Ball High School block (Block 321)
correspondences.why_unambiguous: Av. H East is a named, labelled 70-ft avenue (both sheets print '70'' in its mouth) - five times wider than the 20-ft alleys, so it cannot be confused with an alley. It is the FIRST of only two interior avenue crossings along the shared seam; one block east is Av. I East, 1050 px away. The block on the up-page/north-west side of this corner is the Ball High School block (321) and the block north-east is the Synagogue block (261) - both unmistakable.

correspondences.feature: West corner of the 20-ft alley mouth east of Av. I East, on the NORTH line of 22nd Street

correspondences.feature: Hydrant on the north side of 22nd St at the mid-block alley, beside the 20-in./16-in./12-in. water-main junction
correspondences.why_unambiguous: Exactly three hydrants are drawn along 22nd St on each sheet, in the same left-to-right pattern, each sitting just east of an alley water-pipe line on the north side of the street. NOTE: the hydrant SYMBOL is placed by eye and its position differs between the two sheets by up to 17 px - the corner points are far better. This particular one is pinned by the unique 20-in. main junction.
